## What it is

**Street maps of your region that work with no internet.** The map is one `.pmtiles` file: OpenStreetMap vector tiles cut out of the public [Protomaps](https://docs.protomaps.com/) daily build. The browser draws it with MapLibre GL JS and the Protomaps basemap style, which includes place names, roads, paths, buildings, water and land use. It is the maps part of the **Offline Knowledge** bundle (REC-NOMAD-01), and fits the field and greenhouse nodes (TAXONOMY `field`/maps).

**Licence:** the packaged upstream is [go-pmtiles](https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles), `BSD-3-Clause`, Market class **L1** (license-matrix row "go-pmtiles"). The viewer is OneMind's own code (Apache-2.0, [`manifests/map_viewer.py`](manifests/map_viewer.py)). The browser libraries it downloads are MapLibre GL JS 5.24.1, PMTiles JS 4.5.0 and @protomaps/basemaps 5.7.2 (all BSD-3-Clause), plus fonts (SIL OFL 1.1) and sprites (MIT) from protomaps/basemaps-assets. **Map data:** the Protomaps basemap is an ODbL "Produced Work" and must show "© OpenStreetMap contributors", which the viewer does on every map ([downloads and licence](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads)).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with two containers sharing the 16 GiB volume `offline-maps-data`. Both run as UID 65532 (the distroless `nonroot` user) with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation and all capabilities dropped.
- **`viewer`** (python 3.14 slim image, standard library only, port 8080):
  - It serves the map page and the archives in `/data/maps` with HTTP range requests (PMTiles is read in small ranges by the browser).
  - On first start it downloads the browser libraries, fonts and icons once, **each checked against a pinned SHA-512 or SHA-256**, into `/data/assets`. A file that does not match is refused and the page says why. After that the box needs no internet.
  - It never writes, renames or deletes a map.
- **`pmtiles`** (`go-pmtiles serve`, port 8081): a Z/X/Y tile API (`/<map name>/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt`) for other map clients. It is also the tool the owner uses to cut a map (below).
- Settings: `language` (place-name language, for example `en`, `es`, `de`) and `flavor` (`light`, `dark`, `white`, `grayscale`, `black`).
- Backups skip the maps and the assets, which can be cut and downloaded again.

## First run

Source: [PMTiles CLI](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/cli) and [basemap downloads](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads).

1. Install Offline Maps from the Market (or with the Offline Knowledge bundle) and approve the action. It installs into `app-offline-maps`.
2. **Add a map.** Find a recent build in [maps.protomaps.com/builds](https://maps.protomaps.com/builds/) (builds are kept for about a week). Pick your area as `west,south,east,north` in degrees, for example from [bboxfinder.com](http://bboxfinder.com). Then cut it out (internet needed once):
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-offline-maps exec deploy/offline-maps -c pmtiles -- \
     /go-pmtiles extract https://build.protomaps.com/20261114.pmtiles /data/maps/home.pmtiles \
     --bbox=-122.52,37.70,-122.35,37.83 --maxzoom=15
   ```
   Only the needed byte ranges are downloaded. Each extra zoom level roughly doubles the size: a town to zoom 15 is tens of MiB, a country to zoom 12 a few GiB. Add `--dry-run` first to see the size.
3. Open the map:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-offline-maps port-forward svc/offline-maps 8080:8080
   ```
   then go to http://localhost:8080. With several maps, a picker appears.

To remove a map (the `pmtiles` container is distroless and has no shell, so this uses the viewer's Python):
```sh
kubectl -n app-offline-maps exec deploy/offline-maps -c viewer -- python3 -c "import os; os.remove('/data/maps/home.pmtiles')"
```

## Not done yet

- **Cutting a map is a terminal step.** A Market action ("add map for this area") that the owner approves from the dashboard is the next step. It needs a contract action type for app-specific jobs.
- The tile API's TileJSON needs `--public-url`, which waits for the app proxy's LAN hostname.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: the map is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- No search box (geocoding): finding a place by name offline needs a separate index.
